questions.explain: Pressure is the force acting on each unit of area.

questions.prompt: A box weighing 600 N rests on an area of 200 cm². What pressure does it exert?
A 500 N student stands on one foot with an area of 125 cm². What is the pressure on the floor?
An elephant weighs 40 000 N. Each of its 4 feet has an area of 1000 cm². What pressure does it put on the ground?
questions.explain: 40 000 ÷ 4000 = 10 N/cm². A person on a stiletto heel (about 450 N/cm²) presses much harder!

questions.prompt: Is each design meant to INCREASE or REDUCE pressure?
questions.explain: Small area → big pressure (cutting, piercing). Large area → small pressure (comfort, not sinking).

questions.prompt: Why can a person lie on a bed of 1000 nails without getting hurt?
options: The weight is shared by many nails, so the pressure from each is small
questions.explain: Big total area → small pressure at each point.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of pressure, 1 N/m², is called the…
questions.explain: 1 pascal (Pa) = 1 N/m², named after Blaise Pascal.

questions.prompt: Students in India often carry school bags weighing 5–8 kg. Using ideas about pressure, suggest a bag design that is kinder to shoulders, and one non-design solution.
questions.modelAnswer: Use wide, padded straps so the force is spread over a larger area of the shoulder, giving lower pressure. Use two straps rather than one to share the weight, and add a waist belt so the hips take some load. A non-design solution is to reduce the weight itself: lockers at school, digital textbooks or timetables so only needed books are carried.
rubric: Wide or padded straps spread force over a larger area
Two straps or a waist belt share the load
A non-design idea to reduce the force (weight)
questions.explain: Pressure is reduced by increasing area OR reducing force.
